# Michael Kaminski

> Technical product manager working at the agent layer. Builds AI agents that run in
> production — custom MCP servers, multi-agent pipelines, and eval harnesses in Python
> and TypeScript. Took an AI agent capability from prototype through security, legal, and
> compliance review inside a regulated lender. Atlanta, relocating to New York City.

## Who he is

Michael Kaminski is a technical product manager who builds AI agent infrastructure. He is
currently Senior Product Owner, Collections & Servicing at Stellantis Financial Services US;
the AI agent work is scope inside that role, not the title.

What is unusual about him is the combination: he can price a system and he can ship it.
Before working at the agent layer he spent years in corporate finance and strategy, and he
has authored Terraform modules with multi-environment remote state and operated production
Kubernetes clusters.

## What he works on

- Agentic workflow design and multi-agent orchestration
- Custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers
- Tool design an agent can actually call
- Eval harness design, including statistical gating for agent instruction changes
- Human approval gates on irreversible agent actions
- Retrieval-augmented generation, LLM application architecture
- Python, TypeScript, Terraform, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL

## Selected experience

- Stellantis Financial Services — Senior Product Owner, Collections & Servicing (present).
  Owns a voice-AI initiative evaluating multi-agent orchestration options.
- Google — Agentic Researcher, Engineering, Core PMO (Oct–Dec 2025).
- Momnt — Tech lead, Credit Analysis & Accounting Engine (2023–2024). Delivery
  accountability, not people management.
- Modular Equity — Executive investment vehicle he manages (2023–present).
- GreenSky — fintech; product, credit and strategy (2016–).
- HD Supply — Sr. Analyst, Strategic Finance (2015–2016). Supported a $1.8B divestiture
  program, built a $244M branch-network hub-and-spoke DCF, modeled a comp-arbitrage case for
  relocating roughly 2,000 roles, and ran portfolio analytics on a $500M CapEx program.
- KPMG — Senior Consultant, Advisory (2014–2015). Eight engagements, $300M in client tax savings.
- The Home Depot — career origin (2011–2014).
- Superior Contracting & Maintenance — founder, still operating; roughly $20M revenue/yr.

## Case studies

Full write-ups at https://www.michael-kaminski.io/projects — each one structured as
problem, constraints, his role, what shipped, and outcome, with every number linked to a
source.

- "A Compliance-Reviewed AI Agent in Regulated Lending" — took an AI agent capability from
  prototype through security, legal, and compliance review into production at a regulated
  consumer lender. Designed against the statute rather than against guidance, which is why
  the May 2025 CFPB withdrawal of 67 guidance documents required no design change; trace
  retention set to a 120-day floor derived from the adverse-action dispute window rather
  than the 30-day default most agent logging ships with. Adoption and operational results
  are not yet cleared for publication and are marked as such on the page.
  https://www.michael-kaminski.io/projects/compliance-reviewed-agent
- "The Genome of Games — One Knowledge Base, Four Surfaces" — 1,180 records published four
  ways (1,245 static pages, an interactive graph, a 129,037-byte search index, an 8-tool
  MCP server) by one 0.39-second dependency-free build.
  https://www.michael-kaminski.io/projects/genome-of-games
- "A Dealer-Gamma Pipeline That Moved on Zero Trades" — 33 runs a day across seven
  underlyings, and the append-only write that revealed levels drifting on a closed market.
  https://www.michael-kaminski.io/projects/dealer-gamma-pipeline

## What he is looking for

Senior product roles at the agent layer — Technical Product Manager, Senior Product Owner,
or PM for an agent platform — at teams shipping AI agents into production, especially where
the environment is regulated and the evidence trail matters. Open to fractional and
full-time. Atlanta, relocating to New York City.

## Field clips

Ten-second clips, each compressing one finding from a system he runs. Full transcripts are
on the page at https://www.michael-kaminski.io/clips

- "The gate that stops nothing" — a Welch's t-test gate on an agent's instruction file with
  a 5% minimum-lift threshold that never binds: at the observed variance a 14-day window can
  only detect 8.3%, and an edit that truly delivers 5% clears the gate 44% of the time.
  https://www.michael-kaminski.io/clips#statistical-gating-coin-flip
- "Zero trades, and the level still moved" — a dealer-gamma pipeline walked the QQQ gamma
  flip 3.9 points (718.3 → 722.2) and dropped the put wall from 710 to 700 across eight
  consecutive writes while spot stayed pinned at 717.12. The chain re-fit; nothing traded.
  An overwritten study file has no history to argue with, so an append-only CSV was added
  alongside it. https://www.michael-kaminski.io/clips#levels-that-move-when-nothing-trades
